Thanks for the note, Samantha. Appreciate you sending the files — I can see why the portal flagged this. Two quick items: 1) the certificate PDF is missing an authorized signatory title on the signature line (it shows a name but no title), and 2) the legal business name on the certificate differs slightly from the PO ("Lakeshore Ind. LLC" vs "Lakeshore Industries"). Our ingestion rules are strict on name/EIN alignment for blanket resale acceptance.

Short-term workaround: we can accept a notarized affidavit that: (a) declares the purchaser's exemption claim for the transactions in INV-8492, (b) references the invoice numbers and dates, and (c) includes a wet-ink signature with notary seal. The affidavit should also include the EIN or a statement linking the DBA to the legal entity. Please note we require the notary seal on the affidavit itself (image/photo is OK if it's a legible scan).

Action items for your team:
- Upload either an amended resale certificate (with signer title and matching legal name) OR a notarized affidavit that follows the points above.
- If you upload a scanned notarized affidavit, name the file exactly: Lakeshore_Notarized_Affidavit_INV8492.pdf
- If you prefer to send via secure link, reply and we'll provide a temporary, encrypted upload link (48h).

Looping in Vivek from Tax Ops and Hannah from Billing to confirm acceptance criteria and timeline. Vivek/hannah — can we expedite review once they upload?

Hi Samantha (and Naomi),

Thanks for the context. Quick tax ops guidance so your AP team can remediate with the right docs:

Why the certificate was rejected
- Name mismatch: the legal name on the PO must match the payer name on the certificate or we need a clear DBA linkage.
- Signature metadata: our automated ingest checks for a signatory and title; if title is absent the cert goes to manual review and is frequently rejected if no supporting affidavit is provided.

What we accept
- A corrected resale/exemption certificate with signer name + title and the entity name exactly as it appears on the PO, OR
- A notarized affidavit referencing the invoice numbers and asserting resale status for those purchases. The affidavit must be notarized (wet-ink) and include either the EIN or a clear statement linking DBA to legal entity. Scanned PDFs of the notarized paper are acceptable if legible.

Temporary invoice handling
- If you can upload the notarized affidavit by COB on Thu 3/11, we can provisionally release the invoice hold within 48 hours of verification.
- If you cannot get a notary that quickly, we can offer a partial release for urgent shipments up to 50% with a signed payment commitment; however, that requires a corporate AP contact in the US and a PO-level acknowledgement.

Upload and templates
- Template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c (we've placed a notarized-affidavit template there)
- Secure upload: reply to this thread and Naomi will generate a 48-hour encrypted dropbox link.

HubSpot ticket for tracking: HS-78922

Happy to review any file once uploaded — feel free to attach to the thread.

Regards,
